decisions.reason: As an adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display, it is close to our core converting and display know-how, so we can learn from early customer use and improve it with relatively low development risk.

The pegboard-back cardboard display builds directly on our existing paper-based display capabilities and offers a clear merchandising function that our organisation can readily refine and commercialise.
This standard cardboard quarter-pallet display is highly related to our established knowledge base, making it easier to absorb market feedback and keep it as a flexible core offering.
The eighth-pallet format remains within our core cardboard display competence and gives us a differentiated footprint that we can support with existing production and design knowledge.

A wooden display pallet is less aligned with our main paper and cardboard knowledge base, so our ability to interpret results, improve the product, and exploit synergies is weaker than for the other launches.
Although it uses familiar cardboard-display know-how, its media-specific niche limits learning spillovers and makes it a weaker use of resources than broader display formats in our portfolio.
